## Japan’s Tourism Shift: Chinese vs. Western Behaviors

A significant discussion on 4chan’s /jp/ board highlights a 9.6% drop in foreign visitors to Japan in August, driven primarily by a decline in Chinese tourists. The conversation draws sharp contrasts between demographic groups. Chinese tourists are characterized as staying in segregated bubbles, frequenting Chinese-only hotels, and rarely venturing beyond organized tours. In contrast, American and European travelers are dubbed "white incels," preferring affordable Airbnbs in residential neighborhoods.

The thread details specific grievances regarding Western tourists, including blasting video game music, filming TikToks, and causing confusion with recycling protocols. Anecdotes include tourists urinating on toilet seats and the removal of recycling bins in stations and convenience stores in response. Despite the overall decline, the sentiment is largely positive, suggesting Japan has "healed" by shedding its most disruptive mass tourism wave. One user even notes that Russian tourism remains stable, implying not all demographics are dropping.

## Geopolitics: Iran, Houthis, and the Strait of Hormuz

Newsblur feeds report intensifying tensions in the Red Sea and Gulf regions. Yemen’s internationally recognized leader, Rashad al-Alimi, has called for nationwide mobilization against Houthi forces, offering amnesty to defectors as fighting escalates along the coast. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two drones aimed at Riyadh and two ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait, marking a sharp rise in Houthi aggression.

Diplomatically, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to the U.S. to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting a naval blockade and waiving oil sanctions. President Trump rejected the offer, with reports suggesting U.S. airstrikes may resume after the November midterm elections. Meanwhile, military chiefs from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are convening to coordinate defenses against the growing threat to global trade sovereignty.

## The /gg/ Photography Drama: Wet Plate Snobs and cANON

4chan’s /gg/ (Photo, Video, Audio) board is currently dominated by debates over photography gear and film aesthetics, with a particular focus on mocking the "wet plate chud" subculture. Users discuss the realities of historical photography sets versus modern expectations, noting that contemporary shooters often lack experience with older working conditions. Specific gear mentions include Kodak Super-XX film, Fujifilm (derogatorily referred to as "fujislugs"), and various lenses, with one user humorously comparing a lens to a container for *surströmming*.

A secondary drama centers on a prolific poster named "cANON," who dominates a wet plate thread with over 205 comments. Estimates suggest cANON accounts for 25% of all comments in the thread, yet the community dismisses him as a "nophoto gearfag" who fabricates theories based on zero real-world experience. Other posters mock users who spam low-quality snapshots of mundane subjects while claiming divine photographic insight.

## Quick Hits

*   **Sony E-Mount Versatility:** A Newsblur cluster features enthusiasts sharing photos from South Korea using the Sony A7CII, praising the FE/E mount system's compatibility with legacy A and Minolta lenses.
*   **Analog vs. Digital:** The same cluster highlights a contrast in approaches, with one user detailing a setup of Kodak E100D film, a Helios 44M-4 lens, and a ZENIT 12 camera.
*   **Paris Location Debate:** On /rpt/, users debate the aesthetics of Montmartre and Pigalle. @4529005 defends Pigalle as a hub for music stores and local hangouts, while @Chris argues it displays the "worst part of the city," though both agree Paris is cool overall.
*   **Paperclip Minimizer:** Bluesky users engage in a humorous take on AI thought experiments, discussing an algorithm that converts paperclips into staples. @ver suggests pairing this minimizer with a standard maximizer as the optimal solution.
*   **VTuber Nostalgia:** A wave of enthusiastic, all-caps nostalgia sweeps Bluesky regarding Joy. Fan @SOL ☀ sends a "HI JOY!!!!!! I MISS U" greeting, prompting an equally excited reply from dollip💙 doll VTuber: "I MISS U TOO AAAA."
*   **Hell Is Us Delayed:** Rogue Factor has delayed the Nintendo Switch 2 release of *Hell Is Us* from early October to October 27, 2026. The delay is attributed to logistical and distribution issues rather than technical problems, aligning with a major update for Xbox Game Pass and PlayStation Plus. The game, featuring protagonist Rémi battling supernatural creatures with a drone and sword, is being hailed by media as a potential underrated title of 2025.

He said the campaign would restore state institutions and extend government sovereignty across the country, including to the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa. Al-Alimi also offered a general amnesty to Houthi fighters and affiliates who leave the movement and stop fighting or working for it, subject to legal procedures. The appeal followed a sharp escalation in fighting, including Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have also imposed a naval blockade on Saudi vessels. Yemen’s vice president warned that the Houthi advance toward Mokha threatened the global economy; about 12% of world trade passes through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The military chiefs of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met in Riyadh on Friday amid the escalation. @Kagi News - USA — Trump reportedly rejects Iran's seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz — The Wall Street Journal reported, as cited by the New York Post and other outlets, that President Trump rejected Iran’s proposed seven-day plan. The report said Trump told aides U.S. airstrikes were likely to resume after the November midterm elections; the scope of any renewed attacks remained unclear. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran sent the proposal to Washington through mediators. It would require the United States to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observe a ceasefire that includes Lebanon; Iran would then reopen the strait and resume talks on its nuclear program. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian told CBS News that Tehran would honor its commitments if Washington accepted the plan. Highlights: Seven-day sequence: Araghchi said preparatory steps would take four to five days, the strait would reopen on day six and nuclear talks would begin on day seven. Blockade enforcement: U.S. Central Command said it had redirected 122 commercial vessels to enforce the blockade of Iran. The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan - Abbas Araghchi Perspectives: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told CBS News that Iran would allow U.N. nuclear inspectors into the country as part of a potential long-term ceasefire deal. ( CBS News ) U.S. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott told Al Jazeera that the door to diplomacy with Iran remained open and that the United States was not the party that stopped diplomacy. ( Al Jazeera ) An Iranian official said Tehran would make no concessions on its nuclear program under the Hormuz proposal. representative_texts: @4530770 - /p/ — /gg/ - gear general — >>4530761 >EVF live view does not show the actual image that will be taken Yes it does. That is the entire point of mirrorless: WYSIWYG (what you see is what you get) If your preview does not match the review, something is wrong with the camera (excepting extreme cases like very short and very long shutter speeds). If what you see in EVF during review does not match your computer monitor you need to calibrate the EVF or monitor, or both. Take a photo of something with full tonal range and colours and have the photo displayed on both the EVF and monitor at the same time, observe and make adjustments until they are matching. Displays shift in colour/brightness over time so a recalibration should be done every couple of years. If you open the the RAW in an editor and it displays very differently from what the camera shows you should get a better RAW editor which actually respects the as-shot settings, or maybe it's just a matter of selecting a proper default profile. RAW software from OEM will generally always match the as-shot camera image.

@4530761 - /p/ — /gg/ - gear general — >>4530734 No anon, it's not the same. EVF is smaller than a laptop screen (which is why Japs hide real EVF specs, like vieving angle or resolution), and EVF live view does not show the actual image that will be taken, only a rough low res approximation. EVF is a tool for focusing and taking acceptable exposure, an augmented viewfinder and light meter, not more than that.
